doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Hospital, Miles Davis and Gil Evans
title: Juilliard visits and living on Park Avenue after John Lewis rescued him
summary: He recalls going to Juilliard rehearsals with Gil, Miles and Mulligan, a Park Avenue patron, and John Lewis pulling him out of the Bowery.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Yeah, that person put it together for, like, Hindemith, maybe. Gil, Miles, some people you don’t know, but Mulligan, we’d all walk up to Juilliard. Those were great, great days. I was lucky enough, because I lived on Park Avenue then. A lady had taken a liking to me.
I was going to say, that’s a pretty high-rent neighborhood, George, especially then.
Oh boy. We’re bringing a video tomorrow. I love those little . . .

There again, there’s that thing that when I could have been – I stayed in the Bowery for a little while. John Lewis rescued me from that. Somewhere along the line, I met this woman. She’s very interested in the arts, gave money to the arts, lived on Park Avenue, and had mental problems. I think I have lived the life.

Oh, a fabulous life, I’d say. You have met a lot of – all the people we’ve talked about in the last part of this conversation, these were all from the ’40s, Bird and Mulligan and of course Gil Evans and Miles.
